components.text: Example: RMB 10,000 of author's fees counts as 10,000 × 80% × 70% = RMB 5,600

footnote: Source: Individual Income Tax Law, Arts. 2 and 6, Implementing Regulations, Art. 6, STA Announcement No. 61 of 2018, Art. 8
notes: What gets pooled is called comprehensive income, and it has four parts: wages and salaries, freelance fees (the law calls them remuneration for personal services), author's fees, and royalties. Look at the right-hand column. Salary counts in full. Freelance fees and royalties count at 80%. Author's fees count at 80% and then 70% of that, so 56%. RMB 10,000 of author's fees counts as 5,600. The middle column is withholding, which uses different rules. A freelance payment of up to RMB 4,000 has 800 taken off, a larger one has 20% taken off, and the rest is withheld at 20%, 30% or 40%. A common mistake is to use the 800 at year end. It only applies to withholding. At year end it is always 80%. One exception: since October 1, 2025, freelance pay through internet platforms is withheld cumulatively. More on that under traps.
